source.text:
Something I think about a lot is this idea that if people didn't NEED to do anything, that means they WOULDN'T do anything, or that their actions would never have consequences - that in an ASI-dominated world, the only actor who could ever matter is the AGI/ASI.

But why do people paint by hand when they have Photoshop? Why do they drive manual cars when they could drive automatics? Why listen to the radio when they have cellphones?

Unless an eventual AGI takes away all human agency, there will still be people doing things to other people, because that's what people do. If you gave me enough money to last the rest of my life, I wouldn't just nothing. If I had a UBI and was frozen at my current level of existence with it, I'd focus on something else. Probably telling stories and entertaining my fellow humans, or maybe just myself. It doesn't amuse me to use the machine to tell stories; I prefer to make them up myself, even if mine are inferior.

The potential outcoems of AI I worry about are the ones that prevent me from doing things I want to do, not the ones where I don't get to do the things I currently have to do but don't want to. And just considering those, there's more than enough to worry about. I already live in a world where most of my existence is shaped by factors outside of my control. My fear is those factors tilting against me in a way that materially impacts my well-being, not just that those things change.
